notes: Nine-storey 2010 white-painted concrete frame with full-height glazed bays and a few recessed balconies; ground: glazed lobby with a door, entry door, and a white garage door at the right. Wall tint re-derived against the warm painted-stucco base so the render reads white-grey (dossier), not pink/cream; height unchanged (LiDAR 26.8 m). The Folsom face's left two-thirds are two full-height glass curtain-wall bays with rounded corners and white mullions (reflective light-blue glass) projecting from the white frame; the right third keeps recessed grey balconies. Bays now clear glass tinted pale silver-blue over an opaque pale blue-grey room/blind backing (kit glassBacking), with 1.1 m mullions so each facet reads as several lights. Now kit glassModel: bright reflective pale silver-blue curtain glass (glass-reflective, untinted: about a third of the sky mirrored) with no backing; darker street glass; balcony guards reflective. Bays and upper glass now glass-sky: a bright pale silver-blue dielectric pane (clearcoat sheet), which cannot drop below its own lit tone. Painted stucco read tan/pink from the street. Wall, frame and bay cheeks now painted-white in a cool tint. A big film-glass shop bay at the NE end, a glazed door group, the lobby double door under a glass canopy, white service doors at the SW end (no garages on this face). The untinted glass-sky bays read cream like the wall; bay and upper glass tinted blue-grey so the stacked glazed bays read as glass. Three projecting glazed bays (NE, centre-right, SW) not two, projecting 1.0 m; the lobby canopy opaque pale glass so it reads (the clear canopy vanished). A faint grime pass (weathering.grime 0.07) so the white render is not a flat colour. Bay panes 0.72 m (more white mullion rhythm), projection 1.15, deeper blue glass, varied blind/backing tones. Ground glass is opaque reflective (glass-reflective@a39389) so no interior (seat rows, floor) shows through the shop and door panes.
